newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas mostly steady despite cold forecast.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas mostly steady despite cold forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices held mostly steady Friday despite forecasts for below-normal temperatures in the eastern half of the U.S. this weekend, industry sources said.
Sources attributed the lack of price movement to mild weather in Texas and plentiful storage supplies in the East.
Gulf Coast prices remained in the high-$2.60s to low-$2.70s, which is in line with November 1 indices.
At the New York city-gate, however, prices gained about 10 cents to the $3.05-3.20 area in response to the rising heating demand late this weekend.
Similarly in the Appalachian region, prices rose by more than five cents to the low-$3 area early and then the low-to-mid $2.90s late.
Temperatures in the eastern U.S. are expected to drop to about 10-15 degrees below-normal on Monday, forcing some buyers to tap into storage supplies, which are near full.
In the Midcontinent, where the region anticipated significantly below-normal temperatures this weekend, prices were again unchanged in the low-$2.60s early and then the mid-$2.50s late.
With storage levels only about 70 percent full in the producing region, prices most likely will remain strong in the near-term, market sources said.
In west Texas, Permian prices eased by about five cents ahead of the weekend to the high-$2.40s to low-$2.50s, while at Waha gas traded in the mid-to-high $2.50s.
Due to above-normal temperatures now in the area, demand in the Northwest has weakened, which has alleviated the tight supply situation somewhat, sources said.
